The facts involved in the case, in short, are that the land of lot No. 1 of 'Ka' schedule land of the plaint belonged to Gadadhar, Gaur and Netai; that. before C.S. operation was started Netai died leaving his widow Gyandari Dasya and the C. S. record was finally published in the names of Gadadhar, Gam Chandra and Gyanada Sundari and the land of lot No. 2 of 'Ka' schedule to the plaint belonged to Gadadhar and Gaur in equal share and the same was published in their names in C. S. operation that the lot No. 3 of 'Ka' schedule land belong to Gadadhar, Gaur Chandra, Thakur Das and Netai in equal share' and C.S. record was prepared in the names of Gadadhar, Gaur Chandra Thakur pas and Goyanada Sundari that lot No. 4 of 'Ka' schedule land belonged to Gadadhar, Gaur Chandra, Thakur Das and Netai in equal share of the half of the land and Srecup and Sreedhar had 8 anas share; that the land of lot No. 3 and 4 of 'Ka' schedule land was partitioned before C.S. operation on compromise amongst the co-sharers and by the said amicable partition the C. S. Plot No. 6, 44, 102 and 120 of the lot No. 3 fell in the saham of Thakur Das and the remaining 4 plots lot No.3 and those fell in the saham of Gadadhar, Govinda and Goyanada and possessed the same exclusively and the land of lot No. 4 plot No. 98 fell in the saham of Sreeup and Sreedhar and plot No. 100 fell in the saham of Thakur Das in respect of plot No. 11 and plot No. 99 fell in the saham of Gadadhar and Goyanada who possessed the same exclusively and the saham fell in the share of Gadadhar, Gaur and Goyanada are described in schedule-'Kha' in lot Nos.  3 and 4 and that the lot Nos. 1 and 2 of 'Kha' schedule land are same land of lot Nos. 1 and 2 of 'Ka' schedule land to the plaint; that Thakur Das died leaving two sons Rasaraj and Basanta and Basanta died leaving only daughter Matangini who gave birth a son and Matangini enjoyed the property of her father as life interest; that after the death of Goyanada the life interest in the land of lot Nos. 1, 3, 4 of 'Kha' schedule land vested to Gadadhar and Gaur as reversionary and since Thakur Das died before Goyanada his sons did not get any share in the share of Goyanada; that the land of 'Kha schedule land possessed by Gaur and Gadadhar and Gadadhar died leaving only son Gajendra who possessed with Gaur; that Gaur had no son and only Nirada was his daughter who was married with Gupi Mandal of Monoharpur village and since the husband neglected her Niroda started living at her paternal house and her father Gaur Chandra arranged the marriage of Niroda with Krishna Dad Mohanta of village Prasadpur and thereafter, Niroda gave birth a son, the plaintiff and when the plaintiff No. 1 was aged above 3/4 years Krishna Das Mahanta and Niroda started living with her father in joint mess with the plaintiff and 3/4 years after Gaur died leaving only daughter Niroda and her son plaintiff No. 1 and the interest of Gaur of 8 anas share of1Kha' schedule land devolved upon Niroda as life interest and Niroda possessed the same; that Niroda was illiterate and dependent with Gajendra and possessed the land through him and Niroda and the plaintiff No. 1 maintained themselves with the earning of the said land and during S. A. operation Niroda through Gajendra tried to record the land in her name and after the publication of the S.A. record Gajendra died leaving behind three sons, defendant Nos. 1, 2 and 3 in managing the property and paying rent and performed different jobs of the family; that in 1967/1968 the R.S. operation started and Niroda gave the responsibility of doing the record on the defendant Nos. 1, 2 and 3 handed over all papers to them and the plaintiff No. 1 used to cultivate the land of 'Kha' schedule separately with the ploughs of others and the rest land Niroda used to cultivate through defendant Nos. 1, 2 and 3 used to take the. usufruct of the land from them; that Niroda Bala gifted 52 acre of land from plot No. 119 and 1.16 acres of land from plot No. 97 of Bagdhuna mouza to the plaintiff No. 1 by executing and registering a deed of gift on 12.06.1972 and in 1977 Niroda died leaving behind only son plaintiff No. 1 and the plaintiff No. 1 iterated the property of Gaur Chandra including 2.13 acres of land obtained through his mother by the deed of gift and possessed the same in ejmali with the defendant Nos. 1, 2 and 3 that the plaintiff No. 1 was baisnab by religion and married man and fostered a daughter and for the betterment of the wife and the daughter the 8 anas share of 'Kha' schedule property obtained and inherited by the plaintiff No. 1 through Niroda and Gaur proposed the defendant Nos. 1, 2, and 3 to make partition of the land but they refused to do so on the plea that the land of 'Kha' schedule land was not recorded in the name of the mother of the plaintiff No. 1 and declared that the plaintiff got no right, title and interest in the suit. land and after collecting the record of the suit land the plaintiff No. 1 came to know about the actual affairs of the record that during R. S. operation a small protion of the suit land was recorded in the name of Niroda Bala and the remaining land was recorded in the names of defendant Nos. 1, 2 and 3 of the 'Kha'seheatfelinci during R.S. operation and as such, the R.S. record was wrong and the right, title and interest of the plaintiff No. 1 in 8 anas share of the 'Kha' schedule land did not affect and the plaintiff No. 1 sold some land of 'Kha' and 'OA' schedule land to the plaintiff Nos. 2-7 and as such, the plaintiff was constrained to file the suit. 

 4. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, learned Counsel, appearing for the petitioners submitted that the plaintiffs having succeeded in proving that Kanai Chandra Das is the legitimate son of Krishna Chandra Das by oral and documentary evidence and on the basis of the said evidence the trial Court decreed the suit but the Court of Appeal below on misreading the evidences and misconstruction of the documents dismissed the suit and since the Court of Appeal below having misread the evidence the High Court Division ought to have looked into the matter and non-consideration of the said aspect the High Court Division erred in law. The learned Counsel further submitted that the since the trial Court having found the plaintiffs as legitimate sons of Krishna Chandra Das and the Court of Appeal below without reversing the same dis-missed the suit and the High Court Division committed an error in affirming the same without considering the said aspect. The learned Counsel finally submitted that since Kanai Chandra Das being the legitimate son of Krishna Chandra Das and since Neroda Bala having gifted the suit land in favour of her son by a registered instrument the High Court Division erred in affirming the judgment of the trial Court in not decreeing the suit.
